answerRows.text: • 💬 This is a real Codex terminal capture used to verify
answer-marker highlighting and wrapped continuation rows.
The paragraph deliberately contains enough text to span
several visible terminal rows, allowing the rendering
behavior to be inspected as the terminal width changes.
The answer marker appears only at the beginning of this
response, while all subsequent words belong to the same
continuous paragraph. When the terminal wraps this text,
the continuation rows should remain readable and preserve
the original sequence of words without introducing extra
markers, unexpected blank lines, duplicated content, or
missing characters. This capture provides a concrete
sample for checking where the marker highlight begins and
ends, how the surrounding answer text is displayed, and
whether visual wrapping changes the apparent boundaries of
the marked line. It also gives a useful selection sample:
copying across wrapped rows should retain the paragraph as
continuous text, subject to the terminal’s normal copy
behavior. Narrowing the terminal should produce more
continuation rows, and widening it should produce fewer,
while the content remains identical. The purpose of this
response is to supply that visible terminal evidence
directly, with one leading answer marker and a
sufficiently long uninterrupted paragraph for inspecting
highlighting and wrapping together.
